answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists sybils: each identity locks a refundable bond sized to the transactions it wants to clear, and peers record performance on a shared ledger. New identities start at the bottom and must earn trust through verified work, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fakes pays a bond per identity and gains nothing without real work. Like a vine climbing toward a summit, reputation grows only through sustained honest service, while a delta of sudden identical newcomers triggers extra verification, making forgery expensive rather than free.
